newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big roll in Waste Management.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big roll in Waste Management.

text.p: An investor rolled a sizable position in Waste Management calls out to August from July in some of the heaviest options trading Friday, traders said.
The Waste Management July 30 and 32-1/2 call traded 7,260 and 3,055 contracts respectively, and the August 30 and 32-1/2 call each traded about 7,200.
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said the volume appeared to be an investor moving a July position out to August.
July options expire at the end of next week.
In late trade, Waste Management shares were up 11/16 at 32-11/16 on consolidated volume of more than 2.3 million.
In other trading, an investor bought a call spread and a put spread in BankAmerica Corp options, traders said.
The BankAmerica January 70 and 75 call and the January 55 and 60 put each traded 6,000 contracts.
"It was a 6,000-lot spread," one trader said. "The customer came in and wanted to buy the January 70-75 call spread and also the January 55-60 put spread together."
He said the customer paid 3-1/2 for the spread.
BankAmerica shares were up 5/8 at 67-1/4 in late trading. Nearly 1.5 million shares changed hands.
Elsewhere, options on several technology companies were busy as the sector rallied strongly, led by Dell Computer Corp, which surged 9-1/4 to 137-7/8 on more than 10 million shares.

Analysts pegged the group's rally to bullishness after Compaq Computer Corp's strong earnings and the company's comments Thursday that its new, aggressively low-priced corporate personal computers were not the start of a PC industry price war.
Among the most active options in the sector was Micron Technology Inc, where the July 42-1/2 call traded nearly 11,200 contracts on the Pacific Exchange.
The stock rose 2-3/16 to 44-15/16.

In other action, MCI Communications Corp options were heavily traded at the Chicago Board Options Exchange as the shares fell sharply after the telecommunications company said it expected earnings for the second half of 1997 and going into 1998 would fall short of Wall Street expectations.
The stock, the most active on the Nasdaq stock market with turnover of 33.6 million, dropped 7-3/8 to 35.
The heaviest MCI options activity was on the call side, where the July 37-1/2 traded 5,800 contracts. The July 35 call traded more than 5,000 and the July 32-1/2 call traded 3,830.
Other active MCI calls included the August 35 and 37-1/2 and the October 32-1/2.
The most active MCI put was the July 30, with volume of 2,560 contracts.
